title: The Chapter of the Elements that wept
text:
⟨p.148⟩
59
— The Chapter of the Ele-
59 -ments that wept 59
Once again he said to his disciples: "The garments
of the sons of the First Man wept; they raised up (their cry) three times,
thereafter they fell silent. There is also another fourth weeping
in which they shall weep at the end, and they shall be stilled from their weeping,
and they shall not see them weeping again from this hour onward.
Now the first weeping in which they wept is the time
when they saw the Darkness, the Enemy, hanging extended at a distance against them.
They knew every matter that would befall them; they perceived
what would rise up against them, and would come upon them through him. {8}
-but on account of the Necessity, they hastened in unto {9}him; {10}

ever, since no rest shall reach them from this moment.
But they themselves — the firmaments of the elements — they are the fourth
fourth weeping, being grieved at heart over them with lamentation before them, more
than the other three first weepings; theirs is not {25}

who shall be cut off from the rest, since no rest shall
come to be for them that they may rest there, away from the torment, for
ever.
And the cause indeed of the last going-astray of the souls —
though all the apostles and the Fathers, the revealers
forth of the Good — the prophets of truth — {28}
to every toil, every necessity that confronts them, in order that they might
save (the souls) from the second death — not one of the
apostles all desired to take his recompense in {29};
but they spent their entire appointed-time being in affliction, taking
suffering and crucifixion in their bodies, in order that {30}
